_note: ACCESSIBILITY as contract. A canvas is OPAQUE to assistive tech by construction — there is no view tree to inspect, only pixels — so the semantics are declared or they do not exist. THE LAW. (1) A canvas with any GESTURE handler (on:tap · on:doubletap · on:longpress · on:drag · on:pan · on:pinch · on:rotate · on:swipe · on:press · on:adjust) and neither `a11yLabel` nor `a11yChildren` is a LINT ERROR — code `canvas-a11y-label`, failing `lint_dsx.rb --strict`, not a runtime warning nobody reads. (2) `on:draw` and `on:frame` are NOT interaction: a painted background is decorative. (3) A canvas with no label, no overlay and no handlers is DECORATIVE and hidden from assistive tech — the correct default for a flourish, and the reason the rule can afford to be an error where it does apply. (4) `a11yChildren` declares a semantic overlay tree (the accessible bar-chart pattern): the canvas becomes a GROUP and each child is a real accessibility element with its own role, label and value. (5) A blank label is not a label. The verdict shape here is what all three renderers apply and what the linter enforces — one fold, one rule, three surfaces.

cases.name: a decorative canvas with no label and no handlers is hidden
a gesture handler with no label is the LINT ERROR

lint.message: <canvas> with a gesture handler needs a11yLabel — a canvas is opaque to assistive tech

cases.name: a tap handler with no label is the LINT ERROR

lint.message: <canvas> with a gesture handler needs a11yLabel — a canvas is opaque to assistive tech

cases.name: a gesture handler with a label is a button
a blank label does not count

lint.message: <canvas> with a gesture handler needs a11yLabel — a canvas is opaque to assistive tech

cases.name: a labelled non-interactive canvas is an image
a11yChildren satisfy the rule even without a label
